note_2026_08_12_fee_tiers_and_line_notif:
Second long session the same day, picking up right after note_2026_08_12 (de74fcf) shipped. Five commits landed (db5cff1, 9e0ab21, b75f6fa, 09da6a3, plus a debug pair 012fecb/c6921ef that fully cancel out) and a sixth debug commit (fdc3f9e) is STILL LIVE on prod — see syncStatus.

  (1) TIERED DELIVERY FEE (db5cff1). Replaced the base+per-km formula entirely with a flat fee per 1km distance band, at the shop's explicit numbers: ฿20 (0-2km, shop said '1-2km=20' and confirmed 0-1km should match), ฿30 (2-3km), ฿40 (3-4km), ฿50 (4-5km). lib/deliveryFee.js's calcDeliveryFee(distanceKm, {tiers}) now takes a sorted tier list and DEFAULT_DELIVERY_FEE_TIERS as the fallback; distance beyond the last tier keeps paying the last tier's fee rather than falling to ฿0. lib/settings.js gained 4 new keys (delivery_fee_tier_2km..5km); /admin/settings shows 4 fee inputs instead of the old 'ค่าเริ่มต้น/อัตราต่อกม.' pair. Seeded to prod via NEW scripts/apply-tiered-delivery-fee-migration.mjs --apply (plain key/value upserts, no schema change, no risk window — the old deployed code never read these new keys). The old delivery_base_fee/delivery_per_km_rate rows (30/30, set during de74fcf's session) are still sitting in the settings table, unused, harmless.

  (2) FREE-DELIVERY-AT-฿300 — ADDED THEN FULLY REMOVED, same day. db5cff1 also replaced the old hard '฿300 minimum to unlock delivery' block with an incentive instead (delivery always selectable; free at ฿300+, tiered fee below) — the shop explicitly chose 'ยกเลิกการบล็อก ให้เลือกจัดส่งได้เสมอ' over keeping the block. Then LATER THE SAME SESSION the shop asked to remove the incentive entirely ('เอาสั่งครบ300บาทจัดส่งฟรีออกดีกว่า') and, when asked, chose the simplest outcome: no threshold at all, delivery always charges the tiered fee regardless of order size (b75f6fa). This was a FULL revert, not a toggle-off — freeDeliveryThreshold/qualifiesForFreeDelivery/the settings key mapping/the admin form field/all welcome+method+summary+payment copy mentioning it were deleted from OrderFlow.js, settings.js, orders.js, app/admin/actions/settings.ts and components/admin/settings-form.tsx, in both th/en/zh. Verified locally afterwards: a ฿1,050 cart still charges exactly the ฿20 tiered fee, no promo notice anywhere. delivery_min_order=300 is still sitting in the settings table, now read by NOTHING — harmless leftover, not a bug.

  (3) EXPLICIT GRAB / LINE MAN COPY (db5cff1, same commit as 1-2). Out-of-radius and self-pickup messaging across all three languages now names Grab and LINE MAN by name (replacing a generic 'เรียกไรเดอร์'/the old Lalamove example) on the distance-step warning, the pickup method description, the welcome screen, and the success-page pickup instructions — the shop's literal ask was to 'อธิบายชัดเจนเลยว่า...ให้ลูกค้าดำเนินการเรียก แกรป ไลน์แมน แมสเซ็นเจอร์'.

  (4) RETURNING-CUSTOMER AUTOFILL VIA LINE LOGIN (9e0ab21). The phone-TYPED lookup from de74fcf's session only fires once the customer types 9+ digits — this wires the PRE-EXISTING /api/customer?lineUserId= endpoint (built earlier, only ever used by the legacy unmounted CartDrawer.js) into OrderFlow.js too, as a second, earlier-firing effect keyed on `profile?.userId` (fires whether the login was explicit on the welcome step or picked up silently from an already-logged-in session). Fills phone/name/address if still blank, same non-clobbering rule as the phone lookup; a `lineLookupDoneRef` guards it to once per login and is re-armed in resetFlow(). Verified end to end against a real customer row (0816631054 -> เต๋ / ที่ 90 / ห้า หมู่ 6) using a TEMPORARY `?testLineUserId=` query-param diagnostic (added, tested, fully removed before commit — this exact pattern of 'temp debug query param, deploy, test on a real phone, capture the result, revert' got reused twice more later this session, see (5)).

  (5) THE 'ไม่มีการแจ้งเตือนในไลน์OA' INVESTIGATION — most of this session's wall-clock time, NOT YET FULLY RESOLVED. Symptom: a placed order never posted a message into the LINE OA's own chat inbox (what staff actually watch), even though the customer's OWN order-confirmation card (server pushToUser, via LINE_MESSAGING_TOKEN) kept arriving the entire time — that one fact ruled out a broken/revoked channel token immediately and kept the investigation scoped correctly. The mechanism that's supposed to make an order show up as a new incoming-looking chat message is `liff.sendMessages()` in lib/liff.js (posts the order card INTO the chat as if the customer sent it themselves) — LINE-documented as working ONLY inside LINE's own in-app browser, and needing (a) `chat_message.write` scope on the LIFF channel, (b) that channel's 'Linked LINE Official Account' actually set, (c) a normal personal LINE account (not the OA's own Business ID) that's really a friend of the OA, (d) a current LINE app version. Walked the shop through checking every one of these live, over many screenshots of LINE Developers Console / LINE Official Account Manager / the App Store:
    - chat_message.write — was ALREADY enabled. Not the cause.
    - Linked OA — was blank ('-'). THIS WAS a real, separate bug and the shop fixed it themselves (pointed it at the real OA, @694eccdr/Lovepier.Cafe). Correct fix, but did not alone resolve the symptom.
    - First re-test was invalid: the shop tested logged in as the OA's own Business ID, which is not equivalent to a customer (not a 'friend' of its own OA in the normal sense) — redone with a real personal account, still failed.
    - LINE app version — confirmed already latest (App Store showed 'เปิด', not 'อัปเดต'). Ruled out.
    - A Webhook 401 (SlipOK's own endpoint, https://api.slipok.com/api/line/webhook/71639) surfaced by the shop mid-investigation via the console's own 'Verify' button — explained as UNRELATED and NOT chased further: webhooks carry INCOMING events to a server, sendMessages() is an outgoing client call that never touches the channel's webhook at all; a message it successfully posts would show in the OA inbox regardless of any webhook's HTTP status. Worth the shop fixing separately for SlipOK's own auto-scan feature, but it is not this bug.
    - The actual error, finally: extracted with a TEMPORARY window.alert() debug build (012fecb, reverted immediately after in c6921ef — deployed, had the shop test a real order on their phone, read the popup, reverted within ~10 minutes) — `Unexpected API name`, a LINE-app-NATIVE bridge error, not a JS/config error, occurring even with every item above confirmed correct. Best working theory (NOT fully proven, investigation stopped here on cost/benefit grounds): sendMessages() may require the LIFF to have been launched from an actual in-room/chat context, which a Rich-Menu-triggered launch might not satisfy even though `isApiAvailable('sendMessages')` itself reports true — a LINE platform-level quirk, not something fixable in this codebase.
    - PIVOTED to the robust alternative instead of continuing to chase sendMessages(): `LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO` (lib/lineMessaging.js's pushNewOrderNotification — already existed, was always the intended fallback for exactly this kind of fragility) pushes a plain-text alert directly from the server via LINE_MESSAGING_TOKEN to a specific userId/groupId, independent of how/where the customer opened the page.
    - LEFT UNFINISHED AT END OF SESSION: getting the shop's own userId for LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO needed a second temporary debug build, fdc3f9e — `window.alert('Your LINE userId: '+profile.userId)` in OrderFlow.js, gated behind `?showUserId=1` so it can never fire for a normal customer visit. >>> THIS IS STILL LIVE ON PRODUCTION, NOT YET REVERTED — waiting on the shop to open `lovepier.cafe/delivery?showUserId=1` from LINE, log in, and send back the userId shown. Once received: set LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO in Vercel, redeploy, revert fdc3f9e's alert from OrderFlow.js, then verify with one real test order. See followUps.

  (6) PAYMENT-CONFIRMED FLEX CARD MID-WORD WRAP (09da6a3). buildPaymentConfirmedFlex's thank-you line ('ขอบคุณที่อุดหนุน Love Pier กำลังเตรียมออเดอร์ให้แล้ว') had no natural break point; Thai has no inter-word spaces, so LINE's own Flex auto-wrap split mid-WORD ('ออเด' / 'อร์' across the line break) exactly as the shop's screenshot showed. Fixed with an explicit `\n` after 'Love Pier' — Flex text honors literal newlines regardless of `wrap: true`. Same text appears nowhere else in the codebase (grepped to confirm).

  (7) RICH MENU 'OPENS EXTERNAL BROWSER' — RAISED, PARTIALLY INVESTIGATED, NOT RESOLVED. The shop's original complaint ('ปุ่มback...หายไปแล้ว เหมือนมันเปิด external เบราว์เซอร์') came from a screenshot showing Safari with menu-page-looking content — almost certainly from tapping 'เมนูอาหาร' (a PLAIN https://www.lovepier.cafe/menu link on the rich menu), NOT the 'Delivery' button, which was independently confirmed correct (a proper liff.line.me/2010601364-PyUPQa7l link). Whether 'เมนูอาหาร' (or จองโต๊ะ/โปรโมชั่น/About us, also plain https links on the same rich menu) actually has 'Open in external browser' toggled on was never confirmed or fixed — worth checking in LINE Official Account Manager > Rich menu if this complaint resurfaces.

  (8) PATTERN WORTH REUSING: a `window.alert()` gated behind a URL query param (or firing only in a specific failure branch) is a fast, safe way to see real client-side state/errors off someone's actual phone in production, when there is no remote-debugging access. Used three times this session (012fecb/c6921ef, and fdc3f9e which is still pending revert) — always: deploy, have the person test once, capture the exact string verbatim, revert within minutes. Never leave one live longer than needed, even a query-param-gated one.
note_2026_08_12_line_oa_group_alert:
Tail end of the same 2026-08-12 run. Shop asked again 'ทำไมถึงไม่แจ้งเตือนในไลน์oa' and then 'ทำให้แจ้งเตือนกลับไปในกลุ่มไลน์oa ด้วย ตอนนี้กลับมาเป็นแบบเดิมอีกแล้ว...ตอนแรกก็สามารถส่งการแจ้งเตือนในไลน์ได้แล้ว', with a screenshot of the OA chat showing an order card (LP260812-6276) that HAD arrived.

  (1) THE SCREENSHOT IS A RED HERRING, and this is the thing to get straight before touching anything. There are TWO independent notification paths and they keep getting conflated: pushToUser() sends the Flex order card to the CUSTOMER's own chat (working the entire time, and it's what that screenshot shows — the shop was testing with their own phone as the customer, name 'แก้ว'), while pushNewOrderNotification() is the plain-text alert meant for STAFF. The staff one has NEVER fired even once: its first line is `if (!TOKEN || !TARGET) return { ok:false, skipped:true }` and LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO has been empty in Vercel since the day it was written. So nothing 'went back to how it was' and nothing regressed — the staff alert was never live. Verified this session by reading the empty value out of .env.local and confirming pages/api/orders.js:142 calls it unconditionally on every order. Don't go hunting for a regression here.

  (2) WHAT'S NEW: the shop now wants the alert in a GROUP, not a personal chat. That changes the blocker — LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO accepts a userId (U...) or a groupId (C...), but a group's id is exposed in NO LINE console UI anywhere. The only way to learn one is to receive a webhook event from inside that group. This app had no webhook route at all (grepped: nothing under pages/api or app/api).

  (3) BUILT pages/api/line-webhook.js (6c7c86b) whose entire job is answering 'what is this chat's id'. Replies with the id on the `join` event (the moment the OA is added to a group — unprompted, so the shop doesn't have to know a magic word) and on demand whenever someone sends 'id' / 'ID' / '/id'. Ordinary chatter is ignored, so it can sit in a busy staff group without being noisy. Verifies X-Line-Signature via HMAC-SHA256 when LINE_MESSAGING_CHANNEL_SECRET is set, and deliberately still works without it — the only action it can take is replying via a replyToken that LINE itself issues, so a forged POST has no usable token and can't make the bot message anyone. Always returns 200 (LINE retries, then auto-disables, a webhook that errors — and nothing here is worth that). bodyParser is off because the signature is computed over the exact bytes LINE sent.

  (4) VERIFIED LOCALLY with curl against the dev server, using a dummy token + dummy secret temporarily written into .env.local (restored + checked clean afterwards): GET -> 405; empty body (LINE's own 'Verify' button) -> 200; valid signature + join -> 200 AND a real reply attempt reaching api.line.me (LINE answered 401 on the dummy token, which is the proof the path completes); missing signature -> 401; wrong signature -> 401; valid signature + ordinary Thai chatter -> 200 with NO reply attempted; 'id'/'ID'/'/id'/' id ' all -> reply attempted (4 attempts in the log); 1:1 source -> reports the userId instead. Reply attempts were counted in the server log rather than trusted from the HTTP status, since every path returns 200 by design.

  (5) CAUGHT DURING TESTING, worth remembering: `return res.status(405).end()` makes Next 16 log 'API handler should not return a value, received object' — res.end() returns the response object whereas res.json() returns void. Confirmed it was MINE and not pre-existing by hitting GET /api/orders (same `return res.status(...)` style, no warning). Fixed by matching the codebase's `.json()` form. Use res.json(), not res.end(), in this app's pages/api routes.

  (6) STILL BLOCKED ON THE SHOP, entirely config, no code left to write — see followUps for the exact 5 steps. The one with a side effect: pointing the channel's Webhook URL at /api/line-webhook replaces SlipOK's endpoint (the one already 401ing on LINE's Verify per note_2026_08_12_fee_tiers_and_line_notify (5)). That only disables SlipOK's own in-chat bot features; this app's slip verification calls SlipOK's REST API directly from lib/slipok.js and never touches the channel webhook.
note_2026_08_12_min_order_reintroduced:
THIRD session the same day, picking up after note_2026_08_12_fee_tiers_and_line_notify shipped. One commit (02a7567, pushed) covering two connected asks from the shop, both about /delivery's welcome screen and the delivery minimum.

  (1) WELCOME-SCREEN OFFER BANNER. Shop asked to state on the welcome screen: 'พิเศษสำหรับลูกค้าเมื่อสั่งซื้ออาหารและเครื่องดื่ม ทางร้านมีบริการจัดส่งถึงมือเมื่ออยู่ในรัศมี5กม.' Added as a highlighted note (`welcomeSpecialNote`, same warm cocoa-tinted box style as the success step's waitingDelivery note) between the lead paragraph and the numbered steps, radiusKm interpolated so it tracks /admin/settings automatically. First version had no order threshold in it — the shop then asked to add 'เมื่อสั่งซื้อครบ300บาท' into the SAME banner. Asked explicitly via AskUserQuestion whether that ฿300 mention should be real or just copy; shop initially said 'just copy, not really enforced' and the banner text was updated to say 'ครบ 300 บาท' with no functional change. This was WRONG and got corrected one turn later — see (2).

  (2) THE ฿300 MINIMUM IS BACK, FOR REAL THIS TIME — reverses b75f6fa from earlier the same day, which had fully removed the old hard-block version of this exact feature. The shop looked at the summary screen (screenshot with a red circle around 'ค่าจัดส่ง ฿20') and clarified what they actually meant: 'ท่าทางร้านไม่ได้เป็นคนจัดส่งให้เพราะยอดลูกค้าไม่ถึง 300 ก็ไม่ควรขึ้นค่าจัดส่งไหม แต่ถ้าลูกค้าซื้อครบ 300 บาทค่อยขึ้นค่าจัดส่งคำนวณตามระยะทางเหมือนเดิม' — i.e. a real hard minimum, delivery not actually offered below it, but NO free-delivery incentive attached (unlike the version db5cff1 tried and removed same day) — just a plain block, same tiered fee once past it. Rebuilt end to end, deliberately narrower than the original de74fcf implementation this time (no forced-pickup-only messaging, no min-order line added back to welcomeStep2 — the new banner in (1) already covers that framing):
    - lib/settings.js: SETTING_KEYS.minOrder = 'delivery_min_order' re-added, getShopSettings() returns minDeliveryOrder (default 300 if the settings row is empty — but it never actually is; delivery_min_order=300 has been sitting unused in the table since b75f6fa, so this reconnects to the EXISTING value with no migration needed).
    - pages/delivery.js passes minDeliveryOrder through getServerSideProps -> OrderFlow, same pattern as radiusKm.
    - OrderFlow.js: `belowMinOrder = deliveryMethod==='delivery' && minDeliveryOrder>0 && itemsSubtotal<minDeliveryOrder`, computed at the summary step (the 'method' step where deliveryMethod is picked happens BEFORE menu/items, so this can only be enforced once the cart total is known). Gates the continue button (disabled, matching the shop's literal ask, not just an error-on-click) with an inline amber notice ('สั่งอาหารเพิ่มอีก ฿N ให้ครบ ฿300...') PLUS a one-tap 'เปลี่ยนเป็นรับเองที่ร้านแทน' link that calls setDeliveryMethod('pickup') directly — added because deliveryMethod is chosen two steps earlier and re-navigating back through menu->method to switch would be needlessly slow.
    - THE FEE-DISPLAY BUG, caught by the shop from a screenshot before this was even asked to be built as a hard block: while belowMinOrder, the summary card was still showing 'ค่าจัดส่ง ฿20' and including it in the total, even though the continue button was disabled and delivery wasn't actually happening yet — misleading, and NOT what showing ฿0 would fix either (reads as 'free delivery'). Fixed by moving the belowMinOrder computation before deliveryFee and gating deliveryFee itself on `!belowMinOrder`; the summary's delivery-fee row now shows a plain '—' while blocked and the fee (still the normal tiered amount) only appears once the order clears ฿300.
    - pages/api/orders.js: server-side re-check before computing deliveryFee — `deliveryMethod==='delivery' && s.minDeliveryOrder>0 && itemsSubtotal<s.minDeliveryOrder` returns 400, never trusting the disabled client button alone.
    - app/admin/actions/settings.ts + components/admin/settings-form.tsx: minOrder field re-added to the settings form ('ยอดสั่งซื้อขั้นต่ำสำหรับจัดส่ง (บาท)', 0/blank = off) so the shop can change or disable it later without a code change; the old fee-tiers helper text claiming 'ไม่มียอดขั้นต่ำ' (no minimum) was corrected since it's no longer true.
    - Verified end to end on local dev (LIFF blanked, test-mode distance simulate — see note_2026_08_10 (0) for the technique): ฿150 cart -> fee shows '—', button disabled, notice + switch-to-pickup link both correct; bumped to ฿300 -> fee reappears as ฿20, button enables, total ฿320; switch-to-pickup tested separately -> fee becomes 'ลูกค้าจัดการเอง', address goes optional, button enables at ฿150. No console errors beyond the preview pane's own (unrelated) HMR websocket noise.
    - NOT YET VERIFIED ON PRODUCTION — same gap as every same-day session, no way to drive the real LINE login flow from here. See followUps.

  (3) LESSON: the shop's own screenshots (with the red circle) settle ambiguity faster than asking again — the first AskUserQuestion round ('is 300 just copy or real') got the wrong answer because it was asked in the abstract, before the shop had actually seen what 'just copy' looks like in the live summary screen. When a follow-up request arrives as an annotated screenshot, read the annotation as the actual spec.

  (4) THE GATE IN (2) HAD A HOLE, found by the shop testing a real order: it only ever blocks 'delivery' AFTER it's been chosen (at the summary step), but the 'method' step (before menu) let 'ให้ร้านจัดส่ง' be picked completely unrestricted — a customer could tap it with an empty cart, or just pick 'รับเองที่ร้าน' (pickup) there and never see any block or explanation at all, which is what a shop screenshot showed (a ฿39 pickup order with no min-order messaging anywhere, captioned 'ทำไมระบบไม่อัปเดต'). An AskUserQuestion laying out two fix options (move the method step after menu, vs. gate the existing method-step button by the current cart total) was DISMISSED by the shop ('wait for next instruction') — they then sent a second screenshot of the CORRECT summary-step block already built in (2), captioned 'ตอนแรกที่คุยกันระบบจะทำแบบนี้แต่พอใช้งานจริงกลับไม่เป็นแบบนี้' ('this is what we agreed it'd look like, but real usage doesn't turn out this way') — read as: the block DOES work once 'delivery' is chosen, but customers aren't reliably reaching that state because the method step itself doesn't reflect the rule. Fixed without further back-and-forth, going with the narrower of the two options offered (no step reordering): the method step now reads the CURRENT cart total live (the cart persists across /menu and /delivery, so it's not always empty there — e.g. a customer who added items on /menu before ever starting the wizard) via a new `cartBelowMinOrder` (same formula as `belowMinOrder`, just not scoped to deliveryMethod==='delivery' since it now also gates the option itself). When cartBelowMinOrder, the 'ให้ร้านจัดส่ง' button is disabled (opacity-60, cursor-not-allowed, radio dot suppressed even if some stale state had it selected) and its description swaps to `methodDeliveryLockedDesc` ('สั่งขั้นต่ำ ฿300 จึงจะเลือกได้ — ไปเลือกเมนูก่อน') instead of the fee preview; picking 'รับเองที่ร้าน' is the only option and continuing is unaffected. Symmetrically, a NEW block was added to the summary step (mirroring the existing 'switch to pickup' one): if deliveryMethod is 'pickup', within radius, and the cart has SINCE cleared the minimum, a cocoa-tinted (not amber — this is good news, not a warning) notice offers 'เปลี่ยนเป็นให้ร้านจัดส่งแทน', calling setDeliveryMethod('delivery') directly with no re-navigation needed. Verified all four cross-product states on local dev: empty cart at method step -> delivery disabled with the locked copy, click does nothing; add items to exactly ฿280 -> still disabled/no summary suggestion; bump to ฿560 -> summary shows the switch-to-delivery notice, clicking it flips to delivery with the ฿20 fee and total ฿580 correctly; reload with a ฿560 cart already in localStorage and start fresh -> method step shows delivery ENABLED immediately with the normal fee preview, confirming the gate is a live read of the cart, not a one-time check. No console errors. NOT YET PUSHED as of this note — see followUps.

  (5) UNRELATED THING NOTICED WHILE TESTING (4): starting the wizard with items already in the cart (from a previous /menu or /delivery visit) surfaces a 'resume cart?' interstitial ('ล้างรายการ' / 'ดำเนินการต่อ') between the welcome screen and the distance step — pre-existing behavior, not something this session touched, just hadn't been exercised by earlier same-day local testing because the cart was cleared between each walkthrough.

  (6) (4)'S FIX WAS ITSELF SUPERSEDED MINUTES LATER, before ever being pushed. The shop sent a THIRD screenshot — a pickup order, ฿39, red circle around the whole 'รับเองที่ร้าน' card — captioned 'รับเองที่ร้านก็ต้องอยู่ในเงื่อนไขของสั่งซื้อครบ 300 บาทเช่นเดียวกัน': pickup must clear the SAME ฿300 minimum as delivery, not be exempt. This reverses a decision made all the way back in the original de74fcf session (explicitly confirmed via AskUserQuestion at the time: 'delivery only, not pickup').   (1) HEIC UPLOAD (cbb4d6b). Shop could not upload iPhone photos to events: the image just never appeared. Two stacked causes. First, `app/api/admin/upload/route.ts` resizes with sharp, and the sharp build here has NO HEVC decoder (`sharp.format.heif.input.fileSuffix` is only ['.avif']; encoding hevc fails with 'heifsave: Unsupported compression'), so .heic 500s. Second, EventModal.handleUpload had NO catch, so the 500 was swallowed silently — it looked like 'upload finished, image missing'. Fix: `lib/upload-image.ts` now detects HEIC (mime image/heic|heif OR .heic/.heif extension — HEIC often reports an empty MIME) and converts to JPEG in the browser via heic2any before POSTing; all callers (events, promotions, menu) share this lib. EventModal got try/catch + toast on both the main image and the album loop, plus accept=".heic,.heif".

  (2) BINARY CORRUPTION ON VERCEL (40029ca) — the important one. After the HEIC fix images uploaded but rendered BROKEN, returning HTTP 200. Forensics: fetched bytes started `52494646 efbfbd...` (RIFF then U+FFFD) and the file was LARGER than a real webp. Root cause: supabase-js sends a Node `Buffer` as a raw fetch body, and the Vercel serverless runtime coerces that body to a UTF-8 string, so every byte >= 0x80 becomes EF BF BD. LOCALHOST DOES NOT REPRODUCE IT (undici handles the Buffer as binary) — a clean local test proves nothing here. Fix: pass `new Blob([new Uint8Array(webp)], {type:'image/webp'})` so supabase-js sends binary-safe multipart. The Uint8Array wrap is required because @types/node v26 rejects Buffer as a BlobPart. Applied to app/api/admin/upload/route.ts and lib/menuImport/imageProcess.ts. lib/upload-promotion-image.ts is client-side and already passed a Blob. >>> ANY IMAGE UPLOADED BEFORE 40029ca IS PERMANENTLY CORRUPT AND MUST BE RE-UPLOADED.

  (a) IMAGE FOLDER STRUCTURE — the answer is that it does not matter. classifyImages() in lib/menuImport/imageMatch.ts strips folder names and matches on BASENAME only, and imageClient.ts accepts all three input shapes (a .zip expanded in-browser with fflate, a webkitdirectory folder pick, or a drag-drop that walks entries). So per-category subfolders are fine. The real constraints told to the shop: filenames must be UNIQUE ACROSS ALL FOLDERS (since folders are ignored, the same basename in two categories is a conflict), must equal image_code (or image_file when set), must be .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp (HEIC is rejected at match time, not converted — that is a different path from the event uploader), and must not end in ' (1)'. Recommended the FOLDER picker over .zip: expandZip does arrayBuffer()+unzipSync, i.e. the whole archive in browser memory at once, which will not survive a few hundred phone-sized originals.

  (b) WHY NOTHING SHOWED — three independent gates, all found by reading rather than guessing: categories.is_active=true in lib/db/menuPageData.js (the 10 import categories were seeded false), menu_items.is_available=true (the 21 incomplete rows are forced false), and TAB_SECTION_CATS in components/menu/menuData.js only knew the 7 hand-built categories, so even an active import category had no tab and was unreachable.

  (c) THE DUPLICATE PROBLEM. 6 of the 10 import categories shadow a legacy one (chicken-rice-1/chicken-rice, breakfast-7/breakfast, coffee-drinks/coffee+non-coffee+italian-soda, icecream/ice-cream, cake-bakery/sweets, bar-wine/alcohol); only pasta-western, sushi-roll, bbq-seafood and oyster-bar are genuinely new. Enabling all 10 without touching the old ones would have shown customers two parallel menus. Shop chose REPLACE. Result: 212 items visible (233 minus the 21 incomplete), 60 legacy items hidden.

  (d) WHAT SHIPPED. TAB_SECTION_CATS now defines 10 tabs and each one lists its import category FIRST and the legacy equivalent AFTER, so reactivating an old category later lands it in the right tab instead of creating a duplicate tab. SECTION_IDS and the tab labels are derived from that one map (TAB_LABELS replaced three hand-maintained per-language arrays). MenuExperience.js renders sections from the map in a single loop, replacing SEVEN near-identical hardcoded blocks, and hides any tab whose categories are inactive or have no items (previously such a tab was a dead scroll target, because scrollTo() silently no-ops on a missing anchor). getSrcSet learned the import path menu/<code>/960.webp — it only understood the legacy '-960w.webp' suffix — and imageVersion now flows through menuPageData.js -> buildMenuData -> withImageVersion() as a ?v= cache-buster, which matters because re-uploading an image reuses the same storage path. menuAddOnsForCategory also now answers for 'coffee-drinks' (that is why the drinks section renders 59 rows for 57 DB items: the 2 espresso add-ons).

When the row overflows, justify-center pushes the leading items past scrollLeft:0 where NOTHING can scroll them back — measured at 375px: scrollLeft was already 0 and the first tab sat at -350px. This was latent with 9 tabs and became severe at 12. The dark circle with an 'N' floating over the bottom-left of every page in local screenshots is the Next.js dev indicator, not a layout bug. It is dev-only — confirmed absent from production HTML (grep for 'nextjs-portal' returns 0). Do not spend time chasing it.

The footer tagline is `whitespace-nowrap` inside `overflow-hidden`, so an over-large font CLIPS it rather than wrapping. That is why .footer-tagline's clamp is conservative and the line never fills its box — do not 'fix' the leftover space by enlarging the clamp. The rule is duplicated in styles/globals.css (Next app) and site.css (standalone HTML); change both.

To see /delivery steps 2-6 locally, blank NEXT_PUBLIC_LIFF_ID in .env.local (isLiffConfigured() goes false and handleStart falls straight through to the distance step), then use the distance step's own 'โหมดทดสอบระยะทาง' simulate buttons instead of GPS. Restore .env.local afterwards, and never press the final pay button — it creates a real order and pushes a LINE card.

A percentage `height` (even `height:100%`) resolves against the parent's `height` property, NOT its used height. A parent sized by flex or by `min-height` has `height:auto`, so the child computes to 0 and silently disappears. Stretch it with flex instead, or size it in vh.

Size anything in the LINE in-app browser against viewport HEIGHT, not width. LINE's own chrome eats ~45px, so a layout that just fits at 402x784 in a normal browser is below the fold there; a vw-based clamp gives a tall phone the same cramped band as a short one.

--nav-h is published by whichever chrome is sticky at the top: the site Nav on normal pages, OrderFlow's StepHeader on /delivery (Layout unmounts the Nav there). Anything new that sticks below it must offset by --nav-h, and any new top chrome must publish it and clear it on unmount.
drizzle-kit generate is unusable (snapshot drift); write idempotent SQL under lib/db/migrations/manual/ instead.
The in-app Browser pane fights ScrollStack + Lenis smooth scroll: scrollTo drifts. To screenshot a mid-page section, hide the other .scroll-stack__panel elements and add .is-visible to .reveal.

Reading scrollTop/getBoundingClientRect right after setting a scroll returns the PRE-scroll value, because scroll-behavior is smooth — this reads as 'the pane cannot scroll' and it is wrong. Wait ~1-2s or set style.scrollBehavior='auto' before measuring. Local /menu also reports offsetHeight 0 for real cards mid-HMR; measure on production when the numbers look impossible.
~/.npm has root-owned files — install with `--cache <writable dir>`.

OrderFlow's wizard steps swap in place (no real page navigation), so nothing resets scroll on step change by itself. Any content newly added near the top of a step can render already scrolled past if the previous step was tall enough to scroll. Fixed generally with `useEffect(() => window.scrollTo(0,0), [step])` — keep this if the step machinery is ever refactored.

customers.phone, not customers.line_user_id, is the right upsert key for '/api/orders' — LINE login can fail or be silently skipped (this is even easier to trigger locally, since the LIFF-disabled test trick used to reach steps 2+ never populates lineUserId at all), but phone is always required to place an order. A partial unique index (`WHERE phone <> ''`) is needed since phone defaults to ''.

To send the shop an actual screenshot file (not just view one myself), the in-app Browser pane's `computer` click tool is unreliable on this app (silent no-ops/mis-clicks with no clear cause) and SendUserFile needs a real file on disk anyway. `npx playwright screenshot -b chromium --channel chrome --viewport-size "402,784" --user-agent "<iPhone UA>" <url> <file>.png` reuses the Mac's installed Chrome (no ~150MB download) and produces a real PNG. For a multi-step walkthrough, `npm install --no-save playwright` into the scratchpad and drive it with a small script — but pass `{force:true}` to every `.click()`, because the Next.js dev-mode `<nextjs-portal>` badge intercepts pointer events and blocks normal Playwright clicks even on a clearly visible target.

Playwright's `getByRole('button', {name:'+', exact:true}).click()` silently failed to register on this app's qty-stepper '+' button (no error, no effect) while `Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button')).find(b=>b.textContent.trim()==='+').click()` via page.evaluate worked every time — root cause not confirmed, but prefer the DOM-query form for this codebase's plain-text button style.

liff.sendMessages() can throw a native 'Unexpected API name' bridge error even when chat_message.write scope, the LINE Login channel's Linked OA, and the LINE app version are all confirmed correct — suspected cause is that it needs an actual in-room/chat launch context, which a Rich-Menu-triggered LIFF launch may not satisfy even though isApiAvailable('sendMessages') itself reports true. Don't sink more time chasing this path; LINE_ORDER_NOTIFY_TO (server-side Messaging API push, lib/lineMessaging.js) is the robust alternative — it doesn't depend on launch context, LIFF, or any client-side quirk at all.

A LINE Login channel's 'Linked LINE Official Account' (Add friend option) can silently be unset ('-') even after the LIFF app's own scope and everything else about it is configured correctly — sendMessages() needs it pointed at the real OA to have anywhere to post the message.

Testing an OA's own features by logging into LINE with the OA's own Business ID account is NOT equivalent to testing as a real customer — it isn't a normal 'friend' of its own OA. Must use an ordinary personal LINE account that's added the OA as a friend the normal way.

A webhook returning a non-200 (e.g. SlipOK's endpoint 401ing on LINE's own 'Verify' check) is unrelated to liff.sendMessages() or any client push — webhooks only carry INCOMING events to a server. Don't conflate the two paths when debugging a 'no notification' report.

LINE Flex message text with no natural word-break can get split MID-WORD by LINE's own auto-wrap, because Thai has no inter-word spaces for the wrap algorithm to use — e.g. 'ออเดอร์' became 'ออเด'/'อร์' across a line. Insert an explicit \n at a sensible point; Flex text honors literal newlines regardless of wrap:true.

A window.alert() gated behind a URL query param (e.g. ?showUserId=1) or a specific failure branch is a fast, safe way to read real client-side state/errors off someone's actual phone in production when there's no remote debugger available — deploy, have them test once, capture the exact string, then revert within minutes. Never leave one live longer than needed, even a gated one (see fdc3f9e in syncStatus if it's still there).
